title: Chongqing Gaoke Group Office
materials: High-performance double-curved glass facade system with vertical mullions, plus steel and concrete structural components.
summary_en: The 180-meter Chongqing Gaoke Group Office uses a twisting tower geometry derived from the aurora borealis, producing expressive double-curved surfaces on two principal facades. The glass curtain wall and morphing floor plates turn the tower into a fluid urban landmark.

title: Lè Architecture
location: Yuanqu Street, Nangang District, Taipei City, Taiwan
materials: White ribbed facade system with integrated greenery; the public text does not specify additional material brands or exact assemblies.
summary_en: Le Architecture is a 70-meter office tower shaped by large ovoid looping fins that produce a striated, egg-like silhouette. Computational modeling and environmental simulation were used to optimize the envelope and embed vertical greening into the facade.

title: Shenzhen HJ Land Xiyue Tower
materials: Bamboo-like facade elements over a glass-and-metal commercial tower system; public areas combine textured hardscape and warm-toned finishes.
summary_en: Xiyue Tower translates the sectional logic of bamboo into a vertical mixed-use tower with a porous base, landscape bridge, and vertically integrated business community. The tower’s profile and facade rhythm are driven by a biomorphic, growth-like concept.

title: One River North
materials: Glazed curtain wall, planted canyon terraces, and soft sculpted surfaces integrated into the carved facade void.
summary_en: One River North is a 16-storey residential tower whose glass facade is split by a vertical canyon carved as a habitable landscape. The project merges a geometric tower volume with an erosive biomorphic incision that contains terraces, planting, and water features.

title: Guanyun Qiantang City
materials: Layered glass curtain-wall envelopes; the published text does not specify additional facade materials in detail.
summary_en: Guanyun Qiantang City is a five-tower mixed-use complex whose forms abstract sails and river wind into layered, flowing glass profiles. The ensemble is arranged as a sculptural waterfront skyline with staggered curtain walls and rhythmic horizontal banding.

title: Quzhou Sports Park
materials: Exposed wood-grained concrete column walls, monumental steel roof frame, and glass components in the buried stadium complex.
summary_en: Quzhou Sports Park treats a 30,000-seat stadium as land art, burying most of the program and allowing the roof to read as a hovering halo above the landscape. Concrete walls, daylight openings, and a sweeping steel canopy turn the complex into a topographic civic intervention.

title: Gardenhouse
location: 8600 Wilshire Boulevard, Beverly Hills, Los Angeles, California, USA
materials: White rendered exterior cladding and one of the largest living green walls in the United States at the time of completion.
summary_en: Gardenhouse stacks pitched white residential volumes above a green-wrapped commercial base, replacing the usual apartment block with a clustered hillside-village composition. A large planted facade and second-floor communal garden organize the envelope and shared life of the project.

title: Jiaxing Train Station
materials: Floating metal roof canopy and a restored historic masonry station image integrated into a forest-like public ground plane.
summary_en: Jiaxing Train Station inverts the usual rail-terminal typology by placing most operations underground and letting a low floating roof and planted landscape define the public experience. The project recomposes historic memory, infrastructure, and landscape as a permeable transit-oriented development.

title: UNIC Apartments
materials: Steel, concrete, and brick combined into a white sculptural residential envelope with curved balcony bands.
summary_en: UNIC Apartments is MAD’s first completed Paris project and is shaped as a fluid residential landmark wrapped by cascading terraces. The curved balcony bands and white sculptural facade transform dense urban housing into a continuous organic figure.

title: Baiziwan Social Housing
materials: Prefabricated concrete panels with over 80% prefabrication, plus glass and steel elements in the envelope.
summary_en: Baiziwan Social Housing uses Y-shaped tower footprints, stepped massing, and a second-level floating garden to turn high-density housing into a communal topographic landscape. Daylight access and modular prefabrication directly shape the geometry of the project.
